DIAGNOSIS:
A. KIDNEY, NATIVE, BIOPSY
--   PAUCI IMMUNE CRESCENTIC GLOMERULONEPHRITIS WITH EXTENSIVE GLOMERULOSCLEROSIS AND CHRONIC TUBULOINTERSTITIAL DAMAGE (SEE COMMENT)

KAMBHAM

COMMENT: There is no evidence of immune complex mediated disease.  The biopsy shows a chronic and subacute crescentic process with severe tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis.  Clinical correlation with ANCA serology is recommended.

CLINICAL HISTORY: 15-year-old male with hematuria, hypertension and chronic kidney disease.  Physical examination within normal limits, blood pressure 142/81.  Urine analysis 3+ protein and blood.  Ultrasound of the kidney shows mild increase in renal echogenicity, right kidney size 10.9 cm, left kidney 10.8 cm


OPERATION: Native kidney biopsy

GROSS DESCRIPTION: Three specimens are received labeled with the patient's name and medical record number.

The 1st specimen labeled "native kidney biopsy" is received in formalin and consists of a single pale tan/white elongated cylindrical tissue core measuring 1.0 cm in length and 0.1 cm in diameter.  The specimen is entirely submitted between sponges in a single cassette labeled A1 with and NKID tag.    McDonald (02/11/2013)

The 2nd specimen is received in Zeus fixative and is composed of two cores of tissue measuring 0.5 and 0.2 cm in length.

The 3rd specimen is received in glutaraldehyde and is composed of multiple fragments of tissue measuring 0.2 x 0.2 x 0.2 cm in aggregate.

LIGHT MICROSCOPY: H&E, PAS and David Greene stained sections reveal a single core of renal cortex with overlying capsule.  Approximately 15 glomeruli are seen, of which 11 either globally or near globally sclerosed.  Several of these globally sclerosed glomeruli show disrupted Sukumar's capsule and fibrous crescents.  Two glomeruli have segmental cellular and fibrocellular crescents.  The remaining glomeruli are of normal size without evidence of mesangial or endocapillary proliferation; basement membranes are of normal thickness and contours.  No definite deposits are seen on light microscopy.  The tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis and severe, involving at least 70% of the cortex sampled.  Mild interstitial infiltrates of lymphocytes and occasional plasma cells are seen in areas of atrophy.  Mild arterio and arteriolosclerosis is seen but there is no evidence of vasculitis.

IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE:

Population: Glomeruli

11 glomeruli are identified in the tissue submitted for immunofluorescence microscopy.  Of these, 10 either globally or near globally sclerosed.

ELECTRON MICROSCOPY: Toluidine blue-stained thick EM sections reveal 6 glomeruli, of which four are globally sclerosed.  One glomerulus shows a fibrocellular crescent.  Chronic tubulointerstitial damage is quite prominent.  On ultrastructural examination of two glomeruli, the basement membranes are segmentally thin and lamina dense abnormalities are seen in a patchy distribution.  However, no definite basket-weave pattern of Alport syndrome is identified.  Endothelial cells are unremarkable; tubulo-reticular inclusions are not seen.  An occasional ill-defined density is observed in the mesangium and subendothelial location but no definite electron dense deposits are present.  Podocytes display patchy mild foot process effacement.  The 2nd glomerulus examined shows extensive sclerosis with wrinkling of the glomerular basement membrane.


I have reviewed the specimen and agree with the interpretation above. Bamberg , M.D. Pathologist Electronically signed 02/16/2013

* * *  HISTORICAL DOCUMENT CONVERTED FROM CERNER  * * *    PULMONARY CONSULTATION NOTE     PATIENT:  Tiongson, 99999999  FIN:  [000000]  DOB:  01/06/1997  LOC:  3S     Admitting Service: RheumatologyDate of Admission: 03/05/2013 (HD #3)Admitting Attending: Cidon MD, MichalDate of Consultation: 03/07/2013Requesting Service: RheumatologyRequesting Physician: Michelson, DanaPlace of Consultation: 3S   Reason for Consultation: Evaluate for pulmonary hemorrhage     IDENTIFICATION / CHIEF COMPLAINT: 16yo with pauci immune GN, concern for microscopic polyangitis      HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:   Seldon Tiongson is a 16-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of pauci-immune glomerulonephritis diagnosed on biopsy from 02/10/2013, who presented to the Pediatric Rheumatology Clinic at Courtland  at Stanford on 03/05/2013 for evaluation of pauci-immune glomerulonephritis and determination of additional organ involvement.  Seldon was accompanied to his clinic visit today by his mother and younger sister.  His visit history was facilitated with the use of a Spanish translator.    On questioning, his mother says that Seldon has had microscopic hematuria, found incidentally on multiple routine physical examinations by his PMD starting at approximately the age of six or seven years old.  Per his mother, there was no additional testing done in the past, either laboratory testing or diagnostic imaging, and no referral to a specialist for his microscopic hematuria until approximately the Summer of 2012, at which point he was seen by a new primary care physician, who in addition to the microscopic hematuria, noted that Slavin was hypertensive on routine physical exam.  At that point, Seldon was referred to the Pediatric Nephrology service at Mansfield , where he was seen for an initial visit on 10/21/2012.  Per information provided in these visit notes, it appears that his  blood pressures in 09/10/2012 were 130-134/90-94.  His blood pressure approximately one year prior was 118/68.  At his visit with the Pediatric Nephrology service in 10/11/2012, he had laboratory works noting urine with 3+ protein and 3+ blood, a creatinine of 3.1, a BUN of 37, stable electrolytes, normal albumin, a hemoglobin of 11.5, normal complements, a negative ANA, and a PTH of 256.6.  At that time, his creatinine clearance based on the Quraishi equation was noted to be 41.1 mL/minute/1.73 sq m, and was consistent with stage III chronic kidney disease, if his kidney disease was chronic.  From his visit Dr. Rasouli's impression was that his disease was most likely chronic, due to his anemia and his elevated intact PTH.  Dr. Moreland recommended a renal ultrasound at that time. He was next seen on 10/31/2012.  He had a renal ultrasound performed at that time, which noted that there was a mild increase in the renal echogenicity consistent with medical renal disease.  One small cyst in the left upper pole was noted.  It was also noted that there was a mild increase in echogenicity of the renal parenchyma relative to the liver, and the corticomedullary differentiation was slightly less than normal; no hydronephrosis or hydroureter; a small cyst measuring approximately 7 mm in diameter noted in the upper pole of the left kidney, no other cysts noted; right renal length was 10.9 cm, left renal length was 10.8 cm.  Dr. Clement's impression was, based on his ultrasound and his laboratory work, that his disease process was indeed likely chronic.  Based on the echogenicity noted on his renal ultrasound, Dr. Polga highly recommended proceeding to renal biopsy at that time.  In addition, she started amlodipine 5 mg p.o. once daily for his hypertension, as well as starting calcitriol 0.25 mcg once daily for his renal osteodystrophy.  Of note, he is not on a restricted diet or restricted fluid intake as of that  time.    Summers had a renal biopsy performed at Oakland Children's Hospital on 02/10/2013.  His slides were read by the Pathology department at Stanford University on 02/11/2013.  The report noted pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis with extensive glomerulosclerosis and chronic tubular interstitial damage; no evidence of immune complex mediated disease.  The biopsy showed a chronic and subacute crescentic process with severe tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis; clinical correlation with ANCA serology recommended.    Seldon was next seen on by Dr. Shin on 02/24/2013.  At that point, he had laboratory studies that showed an urinalysis with 3+ protein, 3+ blood, a creatinine of 5.2, a BUN of 59, electrolytes within normal limits, albumin within normal limits, a CRP of 1.4, hemoglobin of 9, sedimentation rate 98, and PTH of 472.  He had a chest x-ray performed on the same day, which was found to be normal, per Dr. Holmgren's note. Based on his renal biopsy findings, Dr. Pinto recommended additional workup of Seldon's disease, including a rheumatology referral, as well as a transplant evaluation.  He was referred to the Pediatric Rheumatology Clinic at Newport News  at Stanford for further evaluation.    Seldon has a past history of exercise-associated asthma from approximately eight months prior to his current presentation.  Per the patient, his asthma was diagnosed by his pediatrician secondary to acute difficulty breathing and wheezing.  He has albuterol and he has Qvar inhalers, although he takes both of these on an as-needed basis.  When he does have difficulty breathing and wheezing, he uses his inhalers and his symptoms improve somewhat. His last episode of difficulty breathing was in 12/11/2012.  He complains of no chest pain, no cough and no cyanosis.  He does have trouble breathing with exercise, which he experienced last the day prior to admission, while he was  practicing for a friend's Quinceanera.  At that time, he was dancing.  He noticed trouble breathing and began to feel dizzy, with an associated headache.  When he ceased activity, his symptoms improved.      REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:  Positive for headache and dizziness, as noted in the HPI.  Positive for recent appetite loss.  He denies fatigue or weight loss.  Positive for fever, approximately two days after his renal biopsy.  Positive for abdominal pain for the past week.  Positive for nausea for one day, one to two weeks prior to admission.  Positive for myalgias.  Positive for polyuria, with the need a urinate approximately once an hour.  Positive for four episodes over the past six months of self-described symptoms of his entire body turning numb.  He says that this will last approximately one to three days, usually worse on the first day and improving over the next two days, until it resolves.  He does not know if there are any instigating factors, and he does not report being ill during the time of any these symptoms.  He denies joint pain or swelling.  He denies oral or nasal ulcers.  He also denies any rashes.    A complete review of systems was performed and other than was noted above was negative.    PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:  1. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:    Solorzano is a 16 yo M with repeated episodes of microscopic hematuria since age 6 or 7 years.  No further investigation was done until the summer of 2012, when Murray's new PCP noted microscopic hematuria in the setting of HTN with SBPs in the low to mid-130s compared to an SBP of 118 a year prior.  He was referred to Pediatric Nephrology at Winston-Salem  and further w/u revealed the following: 3+ hematuria and proteinuria on UA, renal insufficiency with a peak Cr = 5.2 likely 2/2 CKD given the presence of anemia and an elevated PTH, renal US with a small cyst in the L upper pole and otherwise c/w medical renal disease and ultimately renal biopsy on 02/10/2013 showing pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis with extensive glomerulosclerosis and chronic tubular interstitial damage.  Murray was then referred to the Pediatric Rheumatology clinic at LPCH for evaluation and determination of additional organ system involvement and was subsequently admitted.     Switzer was also diagnosed with asthma within the last year after developing difficulty breathing with activity, which is worsening in the past few months (used to go to the gym, play soccer).  He was prescribed Albuterol and QVAR, both of which he uses as needed with incomplete relief.  He also has a diagnosis of seasonal allergies a/w epistaxis and nasal pain.  ROS is otherwise positive for fever x 2 days following renal biopsy,  decreased appetite, dizziness and headache with trouble breathing, which resolve with rest, as well as daily blurry vision in the L eye for the past month, episodes of red and painful eyes, abdominal pain for the past week, 1 episode of nausea 1-2 weeks PTA, polyuria with the need to urinate every hour, myalgias and episodes of total body numbess x 4 in the last 6 months.        Given Murray's asthma and seasonal allergies in the setting of pauci-immune GN, he underwent a CT of his chest (CXR as an outpatient and on admission were both unremarkable) and sinuses to look for e/o vasculitic involvement.  Chest CT yesterday showed scattered, non-specific subcentimeter pulmonary nodules, some of which abut the pleura and are likely indicative of underlying scarring.     Consult question: Are pulmonary nodules infectious in origin and would this prohibit the use of immunosuppresive medications to treat underlying vasculitis? ASSESSMENT / RECOMMENDATIONS:   Murray is a 16 yo immunocompetent M with pauci-immune GN and c/f MPA whose w/u included a chest CT showing scattered, non-specific subcentimeter pulmonary nodules, maybe post-inflammatory and related to pulmonary involvement of his underlying vasculitis.  There is also a possibility that these  lesions are fungal in origin, though his exposure history is not convincing.  Given home near the central valley, Cocci would be most likely.  Histoplasmosis, clasically seen in the Artesia , is lower on the differential.  Should Cocci or Histoplasma be the causative agents, given Murray's currently normal immune system and the absence of infectious respiratory symptoms, the nodules should be walled off and in the setting of immunosuppresion, would not be expected to re-activate and cause illness.  That said, it would be worthwhile to check a Cocci immunodiffusion and Histoplasma antibody prior to initiation of vasculitis therapy.    Thank you for allowing us to participate in Payan's care. ASSESSMENT:    Threlkeld is a 16 year old male with findings consistent with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis with now known renal insufficiency admitted for further work-up of potential multi-organ system involvement secondary to underlying disease process, clinically well-appearing, however with vision complaints, shortness of breath while playing soccer, and declining kidney function, and increased DLCO on borderline elevated which warranted a further evaluation for pulmonary involvement.     Patient has a history of asthma and typically uses albuterol 20-30 minutes prior to exercise, during a soccer game 1 month prior to this admission he experienced shortness of breath during exercise. He could not remember if he used is albuterol prior to this. He also states the last time he had been running or played soccer was in 12/11/2012 and he did not experience these symptoms. He was diagnosed with asthma approximatley 8 months ago.     The patient without current respiratory complaints and CT showing some scattered nodules between 1-3 mm, without ground glass opacities or calcification. This could be completely benign, but the possibility of this representing early pulmonary involvement cannot be excluded. The 6 minute walk that thas done today was within normal limits as well as the PFT's are overall reassuring. We would like the patient to follow up closley with  pulmonary.    This information was discussed today with family along with our Rheumatology and Renal colleagues with a spanish translator in a care conference.      PLAN:    1. Follow up Full PFT's with 6 minute walk in 2 months (hopefully on the same clinic day).  2. Follow up scheduled with pulmonary 05/25/2013.     3. Continue to follow signs and symptoms for respiratory involvement closely. We would like him to follow up with us every 2-3 months, as well as report any new respiratory symptoms.   4. Thanks for obtaining ECHO to evaluate for possibility of shunt or signs of pulmonary hypertension. (within normal limits)  5. Please do not hesitate to call for any further questions.  6. We agree with stopping QVAR and and continue Albuterol 2 puffs prior to exercise and as needed for cough.         [ x ] I have reviewed and updated the Assessment & Plan. CT OF THE CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST:  03/07/2013.  CLINICAL HISTORY:   Sixteen-year-old male with a history of Pauci-immune glomerulonephritis with concern for microscopic polyangiitis disease in the chest.   COMPARISON:  None.  TECHNIQUE:   Helical axial CT images were obtained from the level of the thoracic inlet through the upper abdomen.    Based on a 32 cm phantom, the estimated radiation exposure/slice (CTDlvol  [mGy]) for each series in the exam are:  (9.36).  The estimated cumulative exposure (DLP mGy-cm) is: 336.  FINDINGS:    The visualized thoracic inlet is unremarkable.  There is no concerning thyroid masses.  No supraclavicular or pathological adenopathy.  A normal 3-vessel branching aortic arch is present.  A small amount of residual anterior thymic tissue is present, within normal limits.   The heart is not enlarged.  There is no pericardial effusion or pericardial fluid. The myocardium does appear slightly hyperdense compared to the adjacent cardiac content suggestive of mild anemia.  The trachea, main stem bronchi, and subsegmental bronchi are patent without bronchial wall thickening or bronchiectasis.  There are no endobronchial filling defects noted.  The visualized lung fields are without focal ground glass opacity.  There is no significant areas of pleural thickening or pleural effusion.  There are scattered nonspecific pulmonary nodule seen, some of which abut the pleura, likely representing scars.  OF note, there is a scar seen within the right upper lung apex, series 3, image 47.  Another subpleural nodule is seen measuring up to 2 mm is seen, series 3, image 58.  A punctuate 1 mm left upper lobe abutting the major fissure is seen, series 3, image 88.  An additional nonspecific 1-2 mm nodule was seen abutting the major fissure on the left, series 3, image 137.  A right lower lobe subpleural nodule was seen measuring 2 mm, series 3, image 201.  An additional subpleural scar is seen series 3, image 256.  The most conspicuous nodule is seen within the right lower lobe measuring up to 3 mm, series 3, image 198.  These nodules do not contain any calcification.  There is no calcified mediastinal or hilar adenopathy noted.  The lungs are not hyperinflated and there are no appreciable areas of air trapping appreciated, however this was not an inspiratory/expiratory CT.   The visualized upper abdomen is unremarkable.  The visualized osseous structures are without focal concerning plastic or lytic bony lesions.  IMPRESSION:  SCATTERED NONSPECIFIC SUBCENTIMETER PULMONARY NODULES ARE SEEN, SOME OF WHICH ARE SEEN ABUTTING THE PLEURA AND LIKELY INDICATIVE OF UNDERLYING SCARRING.  THERE IS NO EVIDENCE OF GROUND GLASS OPACITY SEEN TO SUGGEST UNDERLYING PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE.   THESE FINDINGS ARE NONSPECIFIC AND MAY REPRESENT POST INFECTIOUS OR POST INFLAMMATORY NODULES. END OF IMPRESSION. * * *  HISTORICAL DOCUMENT CONVERTED FROM CERNER  * * *    PATIENT NAME:  Larrison, Stephaine  99999999  DATE OF BIRTH:  01/06/1997    CLINIC:  Kidney Transplant  VISIT DATE:  04/16/2013  ATTENDING CLINICIAN:  Joe Jost, MD    PATIENT IDENTIFICATION: Stephaine is a 16-year-old young man, who has a history of chronic kidney disease stage IV secondary to ANCA negative biopsy-proven pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis. He came today with his mom to the pretransplant evaluation clinic for his potential kidney transplant in the future.    HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: Stephaine had persistent microscopic hematuria initially found incidentally on a routine physical examination by PMD when he was approximately six to seven years old (~2002-2003). In mid-2012, he was discovered to be hypertensive as well. He was referred to the Pediatric Nephrology Service at Anaheim  where he was first seen in 10/11/2012. At that time, his labs showed 3+ protein, 3+ blood and a creatinine of 3.1, with a BUN of 37. He had normal complements, negative ANA and a slightly high PTH. Renal ultrasound performed at that time showed a mild increase in echogenicity of the renal parenchyma and corticomedullary differentiation was slightly less than normal with no hydronephrosis or hydroureter. A small cyst measuring 7 mm in diameter was noted in the upper pole of the left kidney, with no other cysts noted. The right renal length was 10.9 cm, the left renal length of 10.8 cm.    At this time, a biopsy was performed in 02/10/2013 at Children's hospital of McLouth  and reviewed by our pathologists. By light microscopy 11 out of 15 glomeruli were either globally sclerosed or near globally sclerosed. Several of them showed disrupted bowman's capsule and fibrous crescents.  Two glomeruli had segmental cellular and fibrocellular crescents. The remaining glomeruli were normal in size without evidence of mesangial or  endocapillary proliferation. The basement membranes were normal in thickness and contour. No definite deposits were seen by light microscopy. The tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis was severe involving at least 70% of the cortex sampled. Mild interstitial infiltrates of lymphocytes and occasional plasma cells were seen in areas of atrophy. Immunofluorescence was positive +2 for C3 segmental sclerosis pattern, and +2 for IgM and segmental sclerosis pattern, but otherwise negative. An EM showed no evidence of Alport's syndrome and the podocytes displayed patchy mild foot processes effacement.In summary, the biopsy was consistent with chronic and subacute crescentic process with severe tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis more compatible with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis.     Serology workup was negative for C-ANCA, negative for P-ANCA, PR 3 was less than 0.2, MPO was less than 0.2, and ANA was negative. He had normal complement levels (C3 of 125, C4 of 42.7), normal IgG level of 744. He had a negative HIV and negative antihistone antibodies.      Stephaine was admitted to the hospital at Clinchco  at Stanford from 03/05/2013 until 03/12/2013, during which time further workup was done including a chest CT which revealed nonspecific subcentimeter scattered pulmonary nodules, which might be indicative of underlying scarring but his spirometry was normal. This was concerning as he also gave a history of new onset of asthma like symptoms from 6 months before. There was no evidence of pulmonary hemorrhage. Ophthalmology showed no evidence of uveitis. Alatorre done on 03/08/2013 was within normal limits. There was no evidence of pulmonary hypertension or pericardial effusion and cardiac function was normal. He also was found to be quite anemic upon admission, with his hemoglobin was in the 8 range, and hence Epogen and iron were started. He also was asked to restart his  calcitriol which he was not taking as prescribed before. He also started Renvela with meals and snacks.  He was also started on vitamin D supplementation. Also at that time, his ESR was found to be high(79).     Pulmonary service was involved. His pulmonary nodules were found to be not secondary to infection, with no evidence of histoplasma or coccidiomycosis.  Pulmonary function tests were within normal limits.  The recommendation from pulmonary and rheumatology service was for him to start on immunosuppression to treat possible pulmonary involvement from his underlying disease. Trombly refused to take steroids because of the cosmetic side effects. Hence he was recommended to take CellCept, which he was not keen on taking either.    Stephaine says that he is feeling fine with no weakness or dizziness.  There was no tiredness or headaches. His appetite was normal. He had normal energy. He has no evidence of hemoptysis, nosebleeds or any other concerning symptoms.      REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: A complete 14-point review of systems was conducted and was found to be negative except as mentioned above.    PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Asthma diagnosed approximately eight months prior to admission.  Seasonal allergies. Suspected ANCA negative pauci-immune glomerulonephritis.    ALLERGIES: No known drug allergies.    MEDICATIONS:  1. Amlodipine 10 mg twice a day.  2. Calcitriol 0.25 mcg once a day.  3. Renvela 1600 mg three times a day with meals.  4. Epogen 4000 units twice a week.  5. Iron 325 mg tablets two tablets twice a day.    FAMILY AND SOCIAL HISTORY: Tierney lives at home with his mother and his younger sister. The family had some trouble with transportation for the visits from Sheffield  to here; however, there are other family members that have been able to assist with this.  Stephaine's main problem is that both he and his family have not been able to understand or appreciate the degree of concern that we have for his renal function, as Stephaine  continues to feel really well. He does not feel that there is need for any medication and no matter how many times we talk to him about the likely progression of his renal disease, he continues to refuse his medication. Today he met up with our social worker and did not seem to be ready for talking about transplantation and dialysis.    LABORATORY VALUES: His most recent laboratory values are from 04/16/2013, showed white cell of 7.4, hemoglobin of 11.9, hematocrit of 35.9, platelets of 291, reticulocyte count of 1.2, ESR 32. Proteinase  3 less than 0.2, MPO less than 0.2, ANA is negative, coccidiomycosis was negative. Histoplasma negative, HIV antibody negative. BK not detected in his urine. VDRL negative. RADIOLOGICAL INVESTIGATIONS: Renal ultrasound from 10/31/2012, shows right kidney measures 10.9 cm, left kidney measures 10.8 cm. Mild increased echogenicity of the renal parenchyma and corticomedullary differentiation slightly less than normal. No hydronephrosis or hydroureter seen. A small cyst measuring 7 cm in diameter noted in the upper pole of the left kidney.    PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:  MEASUREMENTS: Today, his weight is 85 kg. His height is 183.8 cm.  VITAL SIGNS: He was afebrile, with a  temperature of 36.4 degrees Centigrade, and pulse of 59 per minute, blood pressure 144/90 mmHg.  GENERAL: He was alert, interactive. He was not in any acute distress. He looks well nourished, well appearing.  HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic. Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light. No scleral icterus. No conjunctival injection. No periorbital edema. Moist mucous membranes.  NECK: Supple, with no lymphadenopathy.  CHEST: Clear on auscultation bilaterally. No rales, rhonchi, or wheeze.  CARDIOVASCULAR: S1, S2 normal. No murmurs.  ABDOMEN: Soft, nondistended, nontender. No hepatosplenomegaly. No masses. No costovertebral angle tenderness.  EXTREMITIES: Warm and well perfused. No clubbing, cyanosis or edema.  SKIN: No rashes.    ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Tobe is a 16-year-old young man with a diagnosis of ANCA negative pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis.     His renal biopsy is consistent with crescentic glomerulonephritis with extensive glomerulosclerosis and chronic tubular interstitial damage which is pauci-immune, with no immune complexes seen on immunofloresence.  He has negative serology. Further workup in the lungs shows no evidence of pulmonary hemorrhage; however, there were scattered small pulmonary nodules which were nonspecific, and he also had a normal spirometry. The pulmonary nodules were concerning to the Pulmonary service for pulmonary involvement from his underlying disease especially because there was no evidence of them being secondary to infection from histoplasma or coccidiomycosis. He also had a high ESR and with his new history of "asthma" the general consensus was to treat him with some kind of immunosuppression, but Stephaine is pretty determined not to be treated with anything at this point. He does not want to treat with steroids because of the side effects, and he is also not completely aware of the side effects associated with other forms of immunosuppression, including CellCept. He is  going to see the rheumatology service today to talk about this some more. Stephaine also has a history of noncompliance and he is clearly not entirely ready for committing to immunosuppression for life, which he will require after a kidney transplant. At this point, Stephaine has limited understanding of what medical management is required surrounding renal transplantation and is not quite ready to commit to any long term plan right now.    That is because, despite his renal function Vela continues to feel well and carrying on with his regular life despite his poor renal function. It was hard for him to understand why we are starting him on medication, even though during the hospital stay and several clinic visits at Wedron  and here he has been counseled about his significant renal insufficiency which is likely to progress over time. He has been talked to about his more than likely requirement for dialysis or transplantation in the near future. His creatinine has only continued to rise, over the last several months and will likely continue to rise. Stephaine has been told that it is not possible to sustain a healthy living life without adequate renal function. However, despite education about chronic kidney disease and what the future may look for him, Stephaine feels entirely well and he is mentally not ready to accept that he will require renal replacement therapy. Stephaine needs continuous counseling and education about his underlying medical condition and currently is in denial. At this point, based on this, he is not a suitable candidate for immediate preemptive transplantation, and he may require to initiate dialysis first while education and counseling continues.     His renal function, however, is continuing to deteriorate. Today, his creatinine is 6.19 that has increased from 5 in February. This gives him an estimated GFR of 12 mL/minute per 1.73 sq m of body surface area estimated by the Kum equation, with a K coefficient  of 0.41. Stephaine will require dialysis in the near future, unless he gets a preemptive transplantation. We will work with the rheumatology and the pulmonary teams to determine plan for his immunosuppression. We will also assess his compliance. He should be followed up in our chronic kidney disease clinic, to see when Trotter will progress to be requiring dialysis which I anticipate will be pretty soon. Stephaine will be presented in our kidney transplant selection meeting and we will put him on the inactive list so that he continues to acquire time, and we will continue to work with him along with the social work team, so he gets mentally ready for accepting the transplantation.    We will keep in touch with Stephaine and his family pretty closely and monitor his progress. We will continue him on the same amlodipine 10 mg twice a day and we will also start him on the clonidine patch #1. Hopefully, the fact that this is a patch that he does not have to take every day will make it easier for him.  3. Hematology. Sodhi's  hemoglobin is great at 12.2. He has not been taking Epogen for the past two weeks since he ran out of it. His iron studies are also within normal range with a transferrin saturation of 42 and an iron total of 127. We will discontinue the Epogen at this point in time and will monitor his CBC closely to see if at some point in time we need continue it. We will decrease his iron dose to 1 tab twice a day since his iron studies are fine.  4. Bone mineral metabolism. Karl's phosphorus is high. According to him, he does take his Renvela with his meals and tries to maintain a low phosphorus diet. We will increase his Backus  to 3 tabs, 2400 mg with meals, and then 1 tab, 800 mg with snacks. We will also increase his calcitriol to 0.5 mcg once a day, since his PTH is still high.  5. Electrolytes. Shenk exhibits signs of advanced chronic kidney disease. His bicarbonate is low at 20. His potassium is creeping up and is now at 5.1. We would like to start sodium bicarbonate pills to help with acidosis, as well as help with his potassium. We prescribed 2 tabs of sodium bicarbonate twice a day.  6. Rheumatology. We will touch base with our rheumatology colleagues to see if he needs to start CellCept. His previous ESR was high; however, his most recent ESR is 32. Since his underlying diagnosis is unclear at this point, we will touch base with them to determine whether or not we should start him on treatment for his baseline disease.  7. Karl also met with our social worker, Seeberger today, who will try to arrange for transportation for the family once he starts dialysis, to make this easier on them. He also met with Brandy, our dialysis nurse and Sosa, our child life expert, to try and introduce the diagnosis to him and start with the teaching regarding what are the implications of dialysis. We will be in touch with Pasternak again toward the end of this week to schedule a date when he can come in to get his HD catheter placed and to  be started on dialysis. We will repeat a renal function panel as well as a CBC next week when he gets admitted to look at his labs. * * *  HISTORICAL DOCUMENT CONVERTED FROM CERNER  * * *    IP HISTORY & PHYSICAL NOTE     PATIENT:  Segars, 99999999  FIN:  [000000]  DOB:  01/06/1997  LOC:  PAC     Admitting Service: General SurgeryDate of Admission: 06/16/2013 (HD #1)Admitting Attending: Concepcion MD, WaldoPCP: Talley MD, Izaac Feinstein (999-999-9999Primary Resident/AHP: Lavine MD, Quang Tolentino  IDENTIFICATION / CHIEF COMPLAINT: 14y/o male iwth ESRD due to ANCA-negative pauci-immune glomerulonephritis admitted after placement of HD catheter and initiation of hemodialysis. _    SOURCE(S) OF INFORMATION:  patient, mom, chart     HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:      Phoenix is a 16 yo M with hx of pauci-immune glomerulonephritis who presents for placement of HD catheter and initiation of hemodialysis.    Phoenix had persistent microscopic hematuria initially found incidentally on a routine physical examination by PMD when he was approximately six to seven years old (~2002-2003). In mid-2012, he was discovered to be hypertensive as well. He was referred to the Pediatric Nephrology Service at Baton Rouge  where he was first seen in 10/11/2012. At that time, his labs showed 3+ protein, 3+ blood and a creatinine of 3.1, with a BUN of 37. He had normal complements, negative ANA and a slightly high PTH. Renal ultrasound performed at that time showed a mild increase in echogenicity of the renal parenchyma and corticomedullary differentiation was slightly less than normal with no hydronephrosis or hydroureter. A small cyst measuring 7 mm in diameter was noted in the upper pole of the left kidney, with no other cysts noted. The right renal length was 10.9 cm, the left renal length of 10.8 cm.    At this time, a biopsy was performed in 02/10/2013 at Children's hospital of Harmony  which showed extensive sclerosis (see kidney transplant clinic note from 3/21 for complete details on biopsy).    Serology workup was  negative for C-ANCA, negative for P-ANCA, PR 3 was less than 0.2, MPO was less than 0.2, and ANA was negative. He had normal complement levels (C3 of 125, C4 of 42.7), normal IgG level of 744. He had a negative HIV and negative antihistone antibodies.      Phoenix was admitted to LPCH in February, during which time further workup was done including a chest CT which revealed nonspecific subcentimeter scattered pulmonary nodules, which might be indicative of underlying scarring but his spirometry was normal. This was concerning as he also gave a history of new onset of asthma like symptoms from 6 months before. There was no evidence of pulmonary hemorrhage. Ophthalmology showed no evidence of uveitis. Orris done on 03/08/2013 was within normal limits. There was no evidence of pulmonary hypertension or pericardial effusion and cardiac function was normal. He also was found to be quite anemic upon admission, with his hemoglobin was in the 8 range, and hence Epogen and iron were started. He also was asked to restart his calcitriol which he was not taking as prescribed before. He also started Renvela with meals and snacks.  He was also started on vitamin D supplementation. Also at that time, his ESR was found to be high(79).     Pulmonary service was involved. His pulmonary nodules were found to be not secondary to infection, with no evidence of histoplasma or coccidiomycosis.  Pulmonary function tests were within normal limits.  The recommendation from pulmonary and rheumatology service was for him to start on immunosuppression to treat possible pulmonary involvement from his underlying disease. Phoenix refused to take steroids because of the cosmetic side effects. Hence he was recommended to take CellCept, which he was not keen on taking either.     Since this admission, he has been followed by peds rheumatology, nephrology and pulmonology.     Pulmonary recently recommended completing a follow-up chest CT out of concern  for pulmonary hemorrhage, but this was not completed.     Specht's kidney function has continue to deteriorate. His creatinine in March was 6.19, increased from 5 in February and 3 in January. Despite this, Seay is generally asymptomatic. He says he is feeling fine. He is not tired. He does not feel like he has less energy. He is peeing fine. Does not have any headaches, nausea, or vomiting. His appetite is good, though he is restricting himself, because he is not allowed to eat various foods, because of his kidney restriction. * * *  HISTORICAL DOCUMENT CONVERTED FROM CERNER  * * *    PATIENT NAME:  Torpey, Miesha  99999999  DATE OF BIRTH:  01/06/1997    PRIMARY SURGEON:  Favian Fore, MD  ASSISTANT SURGEON:  ANESTHESIOLOGIST:  DATE OF PROCEDURE:  06/16/2013    PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: End-stage renal disease secondary to unknown etiology.    POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: End-stage renal disease secondary to unknown etiology.    PROCEDURE: Placement of permanent hemodialysis catheter.    ANESTHESIA: General endotracheal intubation.    FINDINGS: Patent right internal jugular vein catheter at the junction of the SVC and right atrium. Excellent flow through both ports.    PROCEDURE: Miesha Nicolas Torpey is a 16-year-old young male that has developed end-stage renal disease, now with a creatinine clearance less than 20 mL per minute, and he has evidence of uremia. We explained in detail to him the need to start dialysis and placement of hemodialysis catheter. Intraoperative and postoperative risks and complications, including bleeding, hemothorax, malfunction, the need for reoperation for correction of malfunction. He understood and agreed with the procedure. Previous written consent and preoperative labs.    The patient was taken to the operating room, placed in supine position under general anesthesia. The right anterior cervical area and chest area were prepped with Espino and draped in a sterile manner. Under ultrasound guidance, the internal jugular vein was visualized. Using an 18-gauge needle, we approached the vein with excellent venous return. A guide wire was passed to central position, and then dilated the tract. A Palindrome 14.5 French x 23 cm was placed through a subcutaneous tunnel, leaving the cuff approximately 2 cm away from the skin edge. Then, we proceeded to place dilators and then the sheath, and passed the catheter to central position. There was excellent in both ports. It flushed the saline very well.    We  proceeded to close the skin with 4-0 Monocryl subcuticular suture, and then sutured the catheter to the skin with 3-0 nylon interrupted suture. Then, we placed a Biopatch and Tegaderm. At this point, we proceeded to place a chest x-ray that showed the catheter in good position, with no kinking. The patient was transferred in stable condition to the recovery room.    COMPLICATIONS: None.    CONDITION: Patient stable.    ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS: 5 mL.    FLUIDS: 300 mL of crystalloid. * * *  HISTORICAL DOCUMENT CONVERTED FROM CERNER  * * *    PULMONARY CONSULTATION NOTE     PATIENT:  Kuder, 99999999  FIN:  [000000]  DOB:  01/06/1997  LOC:  3N     Admitting Service: NephrologyDate of Admission: 06/16/2013 (HD #4)Admitting Attending: Northern MD, Gary Hills of Consultation: 06/19/2013Requesting Service: Renal ServiceRequesting Physician: Dudley Clayton, MDPlace of Consultation: 3 N   Reason for Consultation: 14 yo with ESRD with recent placement of HD catheter for initiatiation of hemodialysis, with previous chest CT scan Feb, 2013 demonstrating several small nodules noted along pleural parenchymal interface, along major fissures, and one noted in RLL, with noted changes on PFTs.  The renal service is requesting recommendations regarding start of CellCept given Yechiel refuses taking steroids, and whether a f/u chest CT scan should be obtained now.         IDENTIFICATION / CHIEF COMPLAINT: 14y/o male iwth ESRD due to ANCA-negative pauci-immune glomerulonephritis admitted after placement of HD catheter and initiation of hemodialysis. _     HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: Yechiel is a 16 yo adolescent followed by renal and rheumatology services for diagnosis of ANCA -, pauci-immune glomeruloenphritis, ESRD, now POD#4 for HD catheter placement, with thus far (-) w/u for microscopic polyangiitis. For a more extensive initial presentation and history, please see admission H & P, as well as previous pulmonary consult by Dr. Randy Ashlock in February, 2013.     On Yechiel's previous admission in February, 2013, my colleague, Dr. Reynaldo Foley, was consulted to evaluate for potential pulmonary hemorrhage and  interstitial lung disease secondary to potential microscopic polyangiitis (vasculitis).  The chest CT scan in February demonstrated several small nodules in subpleural regions as well as along major fissures, and one small nodule in the lung parenchyma of the RLL.  There were no  ground-glass opacities, or noted infiltrates likely confirming pulmonary hemorrhage, or significant enlarged nodules, suggestive of a vasculitis process.  In addition, there were no areas of central lobular thickening, or noted air trapping.  He in addition, had normal lung function testing, apart from his DLCO which when corrected for Hbg was 26.0, which was 108%Pred., but when corrected for alveolar volume of 6.07 L was decreased to 3.29 L or 60% predicted, suggesting a possible shunt.  No other abnormalities were noted on Feb. PFTs. In February he also underwent a 6-min walk test attaing 2470 feet, with normal oxygenation throughout the test.  During this hospitalization he also had a normal cardiac echo, with no findings suggestive of pulmonary hypertension.  His immune and rheumatologic workup thus far has been negative for polyangiitis or other autoimmune disease.   He also had a w/u for histoplasmosis and coccidioidomycosis which was also negative.    He was subsequently seen by Dr. Slovak on 05/25/2013 and had a normal physical exam, but had full PFTs which revealed normal lung function apart from mildly decreased FRC, RV, and a DLCO corrected for Hbg which was 31.9, or 136%P, concerning for potential subclinical pulmonary hemorrhage.  He has had repeat pulmonary function testing since he was admitted for his HD catheter which revealed:  ,      Pre Bronchodilator   Actual                      % PredPost Bronchodilator     Actual                    % PredFVC:4.84L94FEV1:3.6282FEV1/FVC:7587FEF 25-75%:2.86L/sec58PEF:8.1588FRCN2:2.37L70FRCpl2.52L74RV:1.37L115RV/TLC:2295TLC:6.21106DLCO: uncorrected24.8ml/min/mmHg106VA:5.46L99MIP (cmH20)MEP (cmH20)  SPO2:  96 %    The testing was limited due to patient discomfort  and  chest pain w/ recent catheter placement.  The patient was only able to complete limited FVC maneuvers.    The testing obtained was technically adequate.  Baseline oxygen saturation is  normal.  Spirometry revealed mild obstruction. Lung volumes measured by plethysmography are normal.  FRC measured by nitrogen washout are essentially concordant with body plethysmography suggesting no significant gas trapping. The DLCO uncorrected for hemoglobin was normal and calculated alveolar volume was also normal. However, the DLCO was not corrected for Hbg.  Compared to previous PFT (05/25/2013) there is decline in flow indices on spirometry likely due to technique noted today.  Additional mild decline in lung volumes were also noted, but overall lung volumes were within normal limitis appart from mild decline in FRC.     A recent CXR on 5/21 revealed normal cardiomediastinal silhouette, with additional low lung volumes without evidence of focal consolidation, pulmonary edema, or pleural effusions.   The chest radiographs since January and chest CT scan in February were reviewed with Dr. Youssef Boyce, Thoracic radiologist, who noted that the small nodular findings mainly along the pleural parenchymal interface and along the fissures were more likely lymph node based and at present not concerning for developing polyangiitis.  At this point she does not recommend a repeat chest CT scan, given his current CXR findings, and minimal findings on chest CT scan. He was admitted on 06/16/2013 for placement of HD catheter and initiattion of hemodialysis. To date, he has not received any immunosuppressant therapy. Rheumatology service briefly evaluated patient to discuss initiation of CellCept therapy given rising ESR and lingering concern active vasculitis especially with regads to pulomnary involvement.     ASSESSMENT:  Reid is a 14yo male with ESRD due to ANCA-negative pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis who to date, has not received adequate immunosuppression for presumed vasculitic process. This, in large part, has been due to refusal on the patient's behalf, to take immunosuppressant therapy - especially those such as steroids, which may alter his physical appearance. However, there is still concern for an active disease process given his elevated ESR (32-->47) and concern for active pulmonary disease evidence by nodules seen on previous chest CT's. His renal disease is now being managed via 3 times a week hemodialysis. Given the above concerns, it is felt that therapy with mycophenolate mofetil is in the patient's best interest. Given the relatively low side effect profile, patient agreed to take this medication. Rheumatology service will continue to  follow.    [ x ] I have reviewed and updated the Assessment. * * *  HISTORICAL DOCUMENT CONVERTED FROM CERNER  * * *    IP DISCHARGE SUMMARY     PATIENT:  Notaro, 99999999  FIN:  [000000]  DOB:  01/06/1997  LOC:  3N     Admitting Service: NephrologyDate of Admission: 06/16/2013 (HD #5)Admitting Attending: Jerath MD, Yehuda Zeccola: Talley MD, Caden Adelman (999-999-9999Attending MD on Day of Discharge: Jass MD, Porte M.  DATE OF DISCHARGE: 06/20/2013 _     ADMITTING DIAGNOSIS: End Stage Renal Disease _     PRINCIPAL DIAGNOSIS: End stage renal disease s/p hemodialysis initiation _     DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:   Chronic kidney disease (585.9)    PROBLEM LIST:   Glomerular nephritis [583.9]     ASTHMA [493]     HEADACHE [784.0]     _     PRINCIPAL OPERATION(S) / PROCEDURES:   hemodialysis _     PATIENT IDENTIFICATION: 14y/o male iwth ESRD due to ANCA-negative pauci-immune glomerulonephritis admitted after placement of HD catheter and initiation of hemodialysis. _     BRIEF HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:  _     DETAILED HOSPITAL COURSE:   History of Present Illness     Curt is a 16 yo M with hx of pauci-immune glomerulonephritis who presents for placement of HD catheter and initiation of hemodialysis.    Galicia had persistent microscopic hematuria initially found incidentally on a routine physical examination by PMD when he was approximately six to seven years old (~2002-2003). In mid-2012, he was discovered to be hypertensive as well. He was referred to the Pediatric Nephrology Service at Murfreesboro  where he was first seen in 10/11/2012. At that time, his labs showed 3+ protein, 3+ blood and a creatinine of 3.1, with a BUN of 37. He had normal complements, negative ANA and a slightly high PTH. Renal ultrasound performed at that time showed a mild increase in echogenicity of the renal parenchyma and corticomedullary differentiation was slightly less than normal with no hydronephrosis or hydroureter. A small cyst measuring 7  mm in diameter was noted in the upper pole of the left kidney, with no other cysts noted. The right renal length was 10.9 cm, the left renal length of 10.8 cm.    At this time, a biopsy was performed in 02/10/2013 at Children's hospital of Oklahoma City  which showed extensive sclerosis (see kidney transplant clinic note from 3/21 for complete details on biopsy).    Serology workup was negative for C-ANCA, negative for P-ANCA, PR 3 was less than 0.2, MPO was less than 0.2, and ANA was negative. He had normal complement levels (C3 of 125, C4 of 42.7), normal IgG level of 744. He had a negative HIV and negative antihistone antibodies.      Vosler was admitted to LPCH in February, during which time further workup was done including a chest CT which revealed nonspecific subcentimeter scattered pulmonary nodules, which might be indicative of underlying scarring but his spirometry was normal. This was concerning as he also gave a history of new onset of asthma like symptoms from 6 months before. There was no evidence of pulmonary hemorrhage. Ophthalmology showed no evidence of uveitis. Dragun done on 03/08/2013 was within normal limits. There was no evidence of pulmonary hypertension or pericardial effusion and cardiac function was normal. He also was found to be quite anemic upon admission, with his hemoglobin was in the 8 range, and hence Epogen and iron were started. He also was asked to restart his calcitriol which he was not taking as prescribed before. He also started Renvela with meals and snacks.  He was also started on vitamin D supplementation. Also at that time, his ESR was found to be high(79).     Pulmonary service was involved. His pulmonary nodules were found to be not secondary to infection, with no evidence of histoplasma or coccidiomycosis.  Pulmonary function tests were within normal limits.  The recommendation from pulmonary and rheumatology service was for him to start on immunosuppression to treat  possible pulmonary involvement from his underlying disease. Shedd refused to take steroids because of the cosmetic side effects. Hence he was recommended to take CellCept, which he was not keen on taking either.     Since this admission, he has been followed by peds rheumatology, nephrology and pulmonology.     Pulmonary recently recommended completing a follow-up chest CT out of concern for pulmonary hemorrhage, but this was not completed.     Weinmann's kidney function has continue to deteriorate. His creatinine in March was 6.19, increased from 5 in February and 3 in January. Despite this, Curt is generally asymptomatic. He says he is feeling fine. He is not tired. He does not feel like he has less energy. He is peeing fine. Does not have any headaches, nausea, or vomiting. His appetite is good, though he is restricting himself, because he is not allowed to eat various foods, because of his kidney restriction.       Hospital Course      Renal:  Patient had HD catheter placed upon admission. He received daily HD for 3 days with appropriate reduction in BUN. This was uncomplicated. He was continued on home doses of calcitriol, cholecaldiferol, sevelamer. Calcitrol, iron and epogen were all transitioned to IV form and given wtih dialysis.  Upon discharge his BUN was 29;  BUN/Cr was 54/8.3 on 06/18/2024.  He will continue HD 3 times per week at an outpatient clinic closer to his home, but for the immediate week post discharge, he will receive HD at LCPH.     CVR:  Patient continued on home dose of amlodipine. His clonidine was increased from #1 to a #2 patch. He also received dynacirc PRN for BP's > 140.  Chest CT is being coordinated for one of his HD visits to LPCH in order to evaluate any vasculitic process.     Heme:  continued home dose iron. His Epo was increased and mixed in with his hemodialysis.    _     PERTINENT LABS AND STUDIES: _     PHYSICAL EXAM:  (Time of Exam: _ )     General: [ x ] no acute distress;  receiving hemodialysis     Head:     [ x ] NC/AT      [ _ ] AFOSF Other: _      ENT / Mouth: [ x ] clear oropharynx         [ _ ] TMs clear    Other: _      Eyes:           [ x ] PERRL     [ x ] anicteric Other: _      Neck:           [ x ] supple      [ x ] no LAD Other: _      Lungs:          [ x ] clear         [ x ] no distress Other: _      Cardiac:      [ x ] reg rate & rhythm  [ x ] no murmurs      Other: _     GI/Abdomen: [ x ] soft            [ x ] non-tender  [ _ ] NL bowel sounds   [ _ ] hepatosplenomegaly   Other: _      GU:                [ _ ] NL external genitalia Other: _      Extremities: [ x ] warm        [ x ] no edema     Capillary refill time: _  Other: _      Neurologic: [ x ] non focal/grossly intact Other:       Skin:              [ x ] no rashes/lesions  Other: _      Musculoskeletal:  [ no ] joint swelling; * * *  HISTORICAL DOCUMENT CONVERTED FROM CERNER  * * *    Pediatric Dialysis - Interdisciplinary Comprehensive Patient Assessment and Plan of Care    PATIENT: Wendel, Huq: [000000] FIN: [000000] DOB: 01/06/1997    Date of Service: 06/26/2013  Referring MD: Ambrosino MD, Delavan   Primary MD: Talley MD, Kressin of 1st Dialysis Treatment: 06/23/2013  Primary Nephrology Fellow: Meng MD, Florence   Primary HD Nurse: Paquia RN, Zito:  _Ziemer is a 16-year-old male who was diagnosed with ANCA negative pauci-immune GN on 02/10/2013. Briefly, Tirado had persistent microscopic hematuria since the age of six to seven years. He presented in 10/11/2012 with a cr of 3.1 and a UA that shwed +3 protein, +3 blood. Workup revealed negative C-ANCA, negative P-ANCA, normal complement levels. MPO was less than 0.2 and PR3 also less than 0.2. ANA was negative. Further workup including a chest CT revealed scattered pulmonary nodules, which are nonspecific, with normal spirometry. No evidence of pulmonary hemorrhage. Ophthalmology exam showed no evidence of uveitis. His ESR was high. Oral underwent a kidney biopsy on 02/11/2013. By light microscopy, the biopsy showed approximately 15 glomeruli, of which 11 were either globally sclerosed or near globally sclerosed. Several of these show disrupted bowman's capsule. The remaining glomeruli are normal in size without evidence of mesangial or endocapillary proliferation. No definite deposits are seen by light microscopy. The tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis is severe involving at least 70% of the cortex sampled.  Immunofluorescence was positive for +2 C3 segmental sclerosis pattern, but otherwise negative.  EM showed no evidence of Alport syndrome, and the podocyte displayed patchy mild foot process effacement. In summary, the biopsy was consistent with chronic and subacute crescentic process with severe tubular atrophy and  interstitial fibrosis, more compatible with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis. Hicks was seen by the rheumatology service who recommanded tx with Cellcept for his underlying disease. He refused steroid tx because of side effects, and hasn't been taking Cellcept either. We have been following Fujii in the CKD clinic. Prater's kidney disease progressed, his cr increased to 8.4, giving him an estimated GFR of 9ml/kg/1.73m2 using the Schwaartz equation with a coefficient of 0.413. He also started to exhibit electrolyte abnormalities and more manifestations of his CKD.     After discussion with Gagnon and his mom it was dedided to initiate HD as inpatient in LPCH. Once we get him to a stable regimen after a couple of weeks we will transition him to Davita dialysis unit in Bunch  which is closer to his home. He will follow with us monthly in clinic.  INTERVAL HISTORY:  Feldstein comes with his mom today for his first comprehensive dialysis clinic visit. He was admitted on 06/16/2013 for placement of an HD catheter and dialysis was initiated the day after. Overall he tolerated the procedure well, with some slight pain that is now improving. He has no symptoms with dialysis and is feeling fine. His main concern is transitioning to Somerdale  to be closer to home.  While inpatient Krasner was seen by pulmonology who repeated PFTs that were normal. His DLCO corrected for Hb was 106 (higher range of normal). His ESR was higher at 46. They recommended a repeat chest CT to evaluate for pulmonary involvement. He was also started on Cellcept 500mg bid._    REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:  Anorexia: Yes  Anxiety/depression: Yes - since health declining/starting HD  Difficulty concentrating: Yes  Headaches: Yes - 2-3 times a week since starting HD  Poor school performance: Yes  Visual Problems: Yes - had vision checked in 03/13/2013 normal exam, blurry vision intermittenly  All other review of systems negative (14 point reviewed conducted). CT OF THE CHEST WITHOUT CONTRAST:  07/16/2013.  CLINICAL HISTORY:   Sixteen-year-old male with a history of ANCA-negative pauci-immune glomerulonephritis end stage renal disease.  Evaluate for previous pulmonary nodules.  COMPARISON:   03/08/2013.  TECHNIQUE:   Helical axial CT images were obtained from the level of the thoracic inlet through the upper abdomen without the administration of intravenous contrast.    Images were obtained utilizing the high-resolution CT protocol in both inspiration and expiration.   Based on a 32 cm body phantom, the estimated radiation exposure/slice (CTDlvol  [mGy]) for each series in the exam are:  (0.07), (5.77), and (0.72).  The estimated cumulative exposure (DLP mGy-cm) is: 256.  FINDINGS:    Right internal jugular present with the distal tip in the right atrium.  The visualized thoracic inlet otherwise demonstrates nonspecific tiny hypodensities seen within the thyroid gland, likely representing regions of small colloid cysts.  All of these are subcentimeter in dimension.  There is no pathological supraclavicular adenopathy discerned.  There is a 3 vessel cervical branching pattern seen to the aortic arch.  No aortic aneurysms are noted.  The main pulmonary artery is not larger than the adjacent ascending aorta. There is a small amount of normal thymic tissue present within the anterior mediastinum.  No pathologic or mediastinal, hilar, or axillary adenopathy is noted. The trachea, main stem bronchi and subsegmental bronchi are patent without evidence of bronchial wall thickening or intraluminal filling defects.  No evidence of bronchiectasis.   The visualized lung fields again demonstrate some nonspecific pulmonary nodules which are noncalcified which appear unchanged compared to previous CT.  There are elucidated as follows:   Subpleural 2 mm scar or nodule seen on series 4, image 42, unchanged compared to prior.  A second focus of subpleural apical nodularity seen on previous CT is no longer present.  Stable 1 mm nodule or intrapulmonary lymph node abutting the major fissure seen on series 4, image 57, previously seen on series 3, image 88.  An additional focus of fissural thickening is seen on series 4, image 77, previously seen on series 3, image 88.  A right lower lobe pulmonary nodule measuring 2 mm on series 4, image 107, unchanged compared to prior when it was seen on series 3, image 198.  Stable 2 mm right lower lobe rounded pulmonary nodule in a subpleural location is seen on series 4, image 109 previously seen on series 3, image 201.  Additionally linear areas of right lower lobe subpleural nodularity is seen likely representing regions of scarring, also unchanged compared to prior CT.  A 3 mm left perifissural nodule is seen series 4, image 84 previously seen on series 3, image 137.  No new pulmonary nodules are seen.  No areas of cavitation.  No ground glass opacities or focal consolidation.  No pleural effusion.  The visualized vessels are unremarkable.   No significant air trapping is seen on the expiratory images.  The architecture of the lung is within normal limits.   Limited visualization of the upper abdomen is grossly unremarkable.  The visualized osseous structures are without areas of lytic or blastic bony lesions.  IMPRESSION:  STABLE PULMONARY NODULES WHICH ARE NONSPECIFIC AND MOSTLY SUBPLEURAL IN LOCATION, NONE OF WHICH ARE NEW COMPARED TO PRIOR.   NO AREAS OF CAVITATION, GROUND GLASS OPACITIES, PLEURAL EFFUSION OR PNEUMOTHORAX.   NO EVIDENCE OF SIGNIFICANT AIR TRAPPING.  END OF IMPRESSION. * * *  HISTORICAL DOCUMENT CONVERTED FROM CERNER  * * *    Pediatric Dialysis - Interdisciplinary Comprehensive Patient Assessment and Plan of Care    PATIENT: Bulman, Doka: [000000] FIN: [000000] DOB: 01/06/1997    Date of Service: 09/17/2013  Referring MD: Bal MD, Varinder  Primary MD: Talley MD, Tejeda of 1st Dialysis Treatment: 06/23/2013  Primary Nephrology Fellow: Crist MD, Claremont   Primary HD Nurse: Paquia RN, Riordan:  _Kaminski is a 16-year-old male who was diagnosed with ANCA negative pauci-immune GN on 02/10/2013. Briefly, Nealon had persistent microscopic hematuria since the age of six to seven years. He presented in 10/11/2012 with a cr of 3.1 and a UA that shwed +3 protein, +3 blood. Workup revealed negative C-ANCA, negative P-ANCA, normal complement levels. MPO was less than 0.2 and PR3 also less than 0.2. ANA was negative. Further workup including a chest CT revealed scattered pulmonary nodules, which are nonspecific, with normal spirometry. No evidence of pulmonary hemorrhage. Ophthalmology exam showed no evidence of uveitis. His ESR was high. Stengel underwent a kidney biopsy on 02/11/2013. By light microscopy, the biopsy showed approximately 15 glomeruli, of which 11 were either globally sclerosed or near globally sclerosed. Several of these show disrupted bowman's capsule. The remaining glomeruli are normal in size without evidence of mesangial or endocapillary proliferation. No definite deposits are seen by light microscopy. The tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis is severe involving at least 70% of the cortex sampled.  Immunofluorescence was positive for +2 C3 segmental sclerosis pattern, but otherwise negative.  EM showed no evidence of Alport syndrome, and the podocyte displayed patchy mild foot process effacement. In summary, the biopsy was consistent with chronic and subacute crescentic process with severe tubular atrophy and  interstitial fibrosis, more compatible with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis. Kristopher was seen by the rheumatology service who recommanded tx with Cellcept for his underlying disease. He refused steroid tx because of side effects. We have been following Ostrowski in the CKD clinic. Kristopher's kidney disease progressed, his cr increased to 8.4, giving him an estimated GFR of 9ml/kg/1.73m2 using the Schwaartz equation with a coefficient of 0.413. He also started to exhibit electrolyte abnormalities and more manifestations of his CKD.   After discussion with Mireles and his mom it was decided to initiate HD as inpatient in LPCH. HD catheter was placed and Stamm inititated dialysis on 06/23/2013. He was than transitioned to DaVita dialysis unit in Casper , closer to his home.   Overall Kristopher is doing well on dialyisis. He still has significant residual kidney function.   INTERVAL HISTORY:  Since we last saw Quinn in clinic he has been feeling fine. He started school so his dialysis schedule had been changed to M/Wed/Fri in the afternoon so he can attend school. Kristopher says that he is feeling fine with dialysis, his energy level is good. Briefly, Tedford had persistent microscopic hematuria since the age of six to seven years. He presented in 10/11/2012 with a cr of 3.1 and a UA that showed +3 protein, +3 blood. Workup revealed negative C-ANCA, negative P-ANCA, normal complement levels. MPO was less than 0.2 and PR3 also less than 0.2. ANA was negative. Further workup including a chest CT revealed scattered pulmonary nodules, which are nonspecific, with normal spirometry. No evidence of pulmonary hemorrhage. Ophthalmology exam showed no evidence of uveitis. His ESR was high. Kenichi underwent a kidney biopsy on 02/11/2013. By light microscopy, the biopsy showed approximately 15 glomeruli, of which 11 were either globally sclerosed or near globally sclerosed. Several of these show disrupted bowman's capsule. The remaining glomeruli are normal in size without evidence of mesangial or endocapillary proliferation. No definite deposits are seen by light microscopy. EM showed no evidence of Alport syndrome, and the podocyte displayed patchy mild foot process effacement. Kenichi was seen by the rheumatology service who recommanded tx with Cellcept for his underlying disease. We have been following Kenichi in the CKD clinic. Kenichi's kidney disease progressed, his cr increased to 8.4, giving him an estimated GFR of 9ml/kg/1.73m2 using the Schwaartz equation with a coefficient of 0.413. He also started to exhibit electrolyte abnormalities and more manifestations of his CKD.   After discussion with Oswalt and his mom it was decided to initiate HD as inpatient in LPCH. Briefly, Willie had persistent microscopic hematuria since the age of six to seven years. He presented in 10/11/2012 with a cr of 3.1proteinuria and hematuria. Rheumatology workup was negative except for high ESR. C-ANCA and P-ANCA were negative, MPO <0.2 and PR3 <0.2, complement levels were normal, and ANA was negative. Further workup including a chest CT revealed scattered pulmonary nodules, which are nonspecific, with normal spirometry. Willie underwent a kidney biopsy on 02/11/2013, the biopsy was consistent with chronic and subacute crescentic process with severe tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis, more compatible with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis. Willie was seen by the rheumatology service who recommended treatment with Cellcept for his underlying disease.   Willie's kidney disase continued to progress. HD catheter was placed and Willie inititated dialysis on 06/23/2013. He was than transitioned to DaVita dialysis unit in Marksville , closer to his home.   Overall Willie is doing well on dialyisis. He still some residual kidney function.   Willie is currently on the inactive transplant list. Our main issue in the past few months has been preparing Willie for transplant, mainly in terms of education and expectation post transplant. Cognitive status and capacity to understand: PT has a remedial understanding of his diagnosis and treatment plan.  PT is beginning to understand the gravity of his condition. MOC also has a basic understanding of condition but refers back to PT for decision making as he is "the man of the house." MOC does not read or write.  It appears that both could benefit from a greater understanding of PT's kidney disease and its long-term effects.     2. Ability to meet basic needs: Family is extremely low income. MOC does not receive any support for her four kids from FOC and is getting by on about $700 a month. MOC utilizes family support as well as foodstamps to make it work. MOC has begun to receive SSDI benefits for PT which has been a tremendous financial help. Family needs to focus on finding consistent transportation as that has been the lead cause of their noncompliance with followup visits that will ultimately clear him for transplant.     3. Ability to follow the treatment prescription:  PT reports following a renal diet and taking his supplements and multivitamins and trying protein shakes. Since he has begun dialyzing, PT has been on time and very compliant in terms of making his apts. PT continues to progress, but remains somewhat indifferent and angry with some providers. He "will do what he needs to do" but team fearful given high risk nature of transplant in  teens, lack of support at home, and attitude of PT. He has made progress and done a good job of taking more responsibility in his medical condition.    4. Mental health history, capacities, and needs for counseling: PT is somewhat stoic but negates the need for counseling. Pung and medical team explained that all teenagers are encouraged to see a counselor and referrals were given to him last month. MOC reports that she has not found any providers. Swer will reiterate importance of therapuetic support.    5. Substance abuse history: none reported.    6. Current ability to cope with and adjust to dialysis: PT has been dialyzing at an outpatient clinic and appears to be attending, however he has not talked to any of his friends about this.PT works with social worker at Davita, Joe. PT has a tough demeanor but will answer questions politely when asked, and appears to appreciate opportunities to vent.      7. Expectations for the future and living with kidney failure and treatment: PT had a kidney transplant evaluation that did not go very well. PT was overwhelmed by the meeting and he and family were not prepared for the referral. Now that he is dialyzing on a regular schedule he would benefit from more information regarding transplant and the transplant process.   MOC has mentioned in passing that they have many extended family members who are interested in donating but is somewhat resistant to ask again. He is blood type B and therefore may wait awhile if receiving a deceased donor txp. He will likely be activated shortly.    8. Educational and employment status, concerns and goals:  PT is a junior in continuation high school and reports doing well in school despite being at a continuation school.  PT danced with his quincenera group in the past, but will not be doing it again this year. MOC somewhat limited in her understanding of PT's school situation.    9. Home environment including current living situation:   Pt lives with MOC and three younger siblings in an apt in Akron . Many extended family members live in the area and in their apt complex.      10. Legal issues:   none known.     11. Financial capabilities and resources: MOC receives $700 dollars a month and relies on extended family for support. MOC is unemployed but has her hands full as a single mom of four children ages 16-4.     12. Access to available community resources: Swer connected PT and MOC to David Villavicencio for CCS reimbursement for transportation and helped the family fill out logs this month. He has been referred to MAW but appears somewhat uninterested at this point.     13. Eligibility for federal, state and/or local resources: SSI, medi-cal and CCS.

SOCIAL SERVICES TRANSPLANT ASSESSMENT          NAME: Portia Nicolas Liang  MRN: [000000]  DOB: 01/06/1997LOC:     Seen by SW this month: yes    Plan for next Psychosocial Assessment: Reassess monthly    Referrals to outside agencies/resources: no    Outside agencies/resources Details:n/a    Age appropriate recreation/activities: yes    Seen by counselor/psychologist/asychiatrist: no    KDQOL-36 completed (Pt> 18 yrs old): no    HRQOL completed (Pt <18 yrs old): yes    Patient plans to maintain health insurance (If >17 yrs old): yes    1. Cognitive status and capacity to understand: PT has a remedial understanding of his diagnosis and treatment plan. PT is beginning to understand the gravity of his condition. MOC also has a basic understanding of condition but refers back to PT for decision making as he is "the man of the house." MOC does not read or write. It appears that both could benefit from a greater understanding of PT's kidney disease and its long-term effects.     2. Ability to meet basic needs: Family is extremely low income. MOC does not receive any support for her four kids from FOC and is getting by on about $700 a month. MOC utilizes family support as well as foodstamps to make it work. MOC has begun to receive SSDI benefits for PT which has been a tremendous financial help.     3. Ability to follow the treatment prescription: PT reports following a renal diet and taking his supplements and multivitamins and trying protein shakes. Since he has begun dialyzing, PT has been on time and very compliant in terms of making his apts. PT continues to progress, but remains somewhat indifferent and angry with some providers. He "will do what he needs to do" but team fearful given high risk nature of transplant in teens, lack of support at home, and attitude of PT. He has made progress and done a good job of taking more responsibility in his medical condition. Family working on identifying people to provide  consistent transportation.    4. Mental health history, capacities, and needs for counseling: PT is somewhat stoic but negates the need for counseling. Copperman and medical team explained that all teenagers are encouraged to see a counselor and referrals were given to him last month. MOC reports that she has not found any providers. Swer will reiterate importance of therapuetic support.    5. Substance abuse history: none reported.    6. Current ability to cope with and adjust to dialysis: PT has been dialyzing at an outpatient clinic and appears to be attending, however he has not talked to any of his friends about this.PT works with social worker at Davita, Purcell. PT has a tough demeanor but will answer questions politely when asked, and appears to appreciate opportunities to vent. Team would like him to participate in post-txp psych protocol once transplanted during the time when he was living locally.    7. Expectations for the future and living with kidney failure and treatment: PT had a kidney transplant evaluation many months ago and was not re. PT was overwhelmed by the meeting and he and family were not prepared for the referral. Now that he is dialyzing on a regular schedule he would benefit from more information regarding transplant and the transplant process. MOC has mentioned in passing that they have many extended family members who are interested in donating but is somewhat resistant to ask again. He is blood type B and therefore may wait awhile if receiving a deceased donor txp. He is active on txp list.    8. Educational and employment status, concerns and goals: PT is a junior in continuation high school and reports doing well in school despite being at a continuation school. PT danced with his quincenera group in the past, but will not be doing it again this year. MOC somewhat limited in her understanding of PT's school situation.    9. Home environment including current living situation: Pt lives  with MOC and three younger siblings in an apt in Elizabethtown . Many extended family members live in the area and in their apt complex.    10. Legal issues: none known.     11. Financial capabilities and resources: MOC receives $700 dollars a month and relies on extended family for support. MOC is unemployed but has her hands full as a single mom of four children ages 16-4.     12. Access to available community resources: Swer connected PT and MOC to Zigmund Schor for CCS reimbursement for transportation and helped the family fill out logs this month. He has been referred to MAW but appears somewhat uninterested at this point.     13. Eligibility for federal, state and/or local resources: SSI, medi-cal and CCS.

Cognitive status and capacity to understand: PT has a much better understanding of his diagnosis and treatment plan than he did back in December when he began dialysis.MOC also has a basic understanding of condition but refers back to PT for decision making as he is "the man of the house." MOC does not read or write.     2. Ability to meet basic needs: Family is extremely low income. MOC does not receive any support for her four kids from FOC and is getting by on about $700 a month. MOC utilizes family support as well as foodstamps to make it work. MOC has begun to receive SSDI benefits for PT which has been a tremendous financial help. MOC will start working two days per week when her youngest starts kindergarten and Odette has been working this summer part-time at Wing Stop.    3. Ability to follow the treatment prescription: PT reports following a renal diet and taking his supplements and multivitamins and trying protein shakes. Since he has begun dialyzing, PT has been on time and very compliant in terms of making his apts. He "will do what he needs to do" but team fearful given high risk nature of transplant in teens, lack of support at home, and attitude of PT. He has made progress and done a good job of taking more responsibility in his medical condition. Family working on identifying people to provide consistent transportation. PT has made a lot of  progress and become more communicative with the team.    4. Mental health history, capacities, and needs for counseling: PT is somewhat stoic but negates the need for counseling. Nienaber and medical team explained that all teenagers are encouraged to see a counselor and referrals were given to him last month. MOC reports that she has not found any providers. Swer will reiterate importance of therapuetic support.    5. Substance abuse history: none reported.    6. Current ability to cope with and adjust to dialysis: PT has been dialyzing at an outpatient clinic and appears to be attending, however he has not talked to any of his friends about this.PT works with social worker at Davita, Priester. PT has a tough demeanor but will answer questions politely when asked, and appears to appreciate opportunities to vent. Team would like him to participate in post-txp psych protocol once transplanted during the time when he was living locally.    7. Expectations for the future and living with kidney failure and treatment: PT had a kidney transplant evaluation many months ago and was not re. PT was overwhelmed by the meeting and he and family were not prepared for the referral. Now that he is dialyzing on a regular schedule he would benefit from more information regarding transplant and the transplant process. MOC has mentioned in passing that they have many extended family members who are interested in donating but is somewhat resistant to ask again. He is blood type B and therefore may wait awhile if receiving a deceased donor txp, which swer discussed with PT today. He is active on txp list and swer discussed the unavailability of RMH for the next 15 months and family's likely need to stay in a local hotel post txp.    8. Educational and employment status, concerns and goals: PT will be a senior this fall in high school and reports doing well in school despite being at a continuation school. PT danced with his quincenera group  in the past, but will not be doing it again this year. MOC somewhat limited in her understanding of PT's school situation. Swer encouraged PT to let her know if he needs help navigating the school system.    9. Home environment including current living situation: Pt lives with MOC and three younger siblings in an apt in Fort Lee . Many extended family members live in the area and in their apt complex.    10. Legal issues: none known.     11. Financial capabilities and resources: MOC receives $700 dollars a month and relies on extended family for support. MOC is unemployed but has her hands full as a single mom of four children ages 16-4.     12. Access to available community resources: Swer connected PT and MOC to Dionte Zaks for CCS reimbursement for transportation and helped the family fill out logs this month. He has been referred to MAW but appears somewhat uninterested at this point.     13. Eligibility for federal, state and/or local resources: SSI, medi-cal and CCS.
